name: ne is dropped
explain: The ne of the negative disappears; pas (or jamais, rien, plus) alone carries it.

name: je sais → chais, je suis → chuis
explain: The e of je drops and the j runs into the s, sounding like ch.

name: an e dropped inside
explain: An unstressed e vanishes and the consonants around it collide.

name: tu → t' before a vowel
explain: tu clips to t' when the next word starts with a vowel.

name: il y a → y a
explain: The il disappears; "there is / there are" is just y a.

name: il dropped before faut, paraît, etc.
explain: Impersonal il disappears in front of faut, paraît, vaut mieux, suffit.

name: il / ils → i
explain: The l of il and ils is not heard before a consonant; you hear i.

name: on instead of nous
explain: Everyday speech says on where the page says nous, with a singular verb.

name: question by tone alone
explain: No est-ce que, no inversion: the sentence is a question because the voice rises.

name: qu'est-ce que → kess
explain: qu'est-ce que is said as one short kess; qu'est-ce qu'il as kesk-il.

name: words run together
explain: A final consonant or vowel links to the next word (liaison, enchaînement), so word boundaries vanish.

name: ça for cela
explain: cela is ça in speech.

name: fillers: bah, ben, quoi, genre, hein, euh, ouais
explain: Words the page never prints that fill and shape spoken sentences; ouais for oui.

name: parce que → pasque, puis → pis
explain: Common little words shrink.

name: celui-là → çui-là, cette → c'te
explain: Demonstratives shrink.

name: elle → è before a consonant
explain: The ll of elle is not heard before a consonant.

name: the subject said twice
explain: Speech puts moi je, lui il, ça c'est where the page has one subject.

name: t'inquiète, tu vas pas, etc.
explain: Fixed everyday phrases said in their reduced shape.

name: a vowel swallowed at speed
explain: il est → y est; tu es → t'es; je vais → j'vais; voilà → v'là.

name: oui and non reshaped
explain: ouais, mouais, nan, bah oui, mais non.
